108 CLAUDE.md
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

content.content:
# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

/**
 * Writes app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json: every production URL the new
 * marketing site (app/nxm) serves, for middleware.ts to route there once
 * NXM_ROOT=1. Run after adding/removing a page or a fan-out route:
 *
 *   npx tsx scripts/nxm-live-routes.ts
 *
 * exact    — fixed routes: the SEO registry + every tools/nxm/routes/*.json
 *            fan-out + every location-landing slug app/nxm/[slug] resolves
 *            (the same lists app/nxm/_data/location-landing.ts resolves from)
 * patterns — template routes (one page per DB row: mods, blog posts, …)
 */
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { SEO } from "../app/nxm/_seo/registry";
import { LANDING_SLUGS, REGION_LANDING_SLUGS } from "../lib/marketing/locationLandings";
import { GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS, GENERAL_LOCATION_SLUGS } from "../lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings";

const ROOT = join(__dirname, "..");
const exact = new Set<string>(Object.keys(SEO));
for (const f of readdirSync(join(ROOT, "tools/nxm/routes"))) {
  if (!f.endsWith(".json")) continue;
  for (const r of JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(ROOT, "tools/nxm/routes", f), "utf8")) as { route: string }[]) exact.add(r.route);
}
const SG_LANDERS = ["singapore-web-hosting", "singapore-reseller-hosting", "singapore-forex-vps-hosting", "singapore-dedicated-server-hosting", "singapore-game-server-hosting"];
for (const s of [...LANDING_SLUGS, ...REGION_LANDING_SLUGS, ...GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS, ...GENERAL_LOCATION_SLUGS, ...SG_LANDERS]) exact.add("/" + s);

// app/nxm template routes, as anchored regexes (one path segment per [param])
const patterns = [
  "^/mods/games/[^/]+$", "^/mods/games/[^/]+/all$", "^/mods/[^/]+/[^/]+$",
  "^/blog/[^/]+$", "^/servers/[^/]+$",
];

const out = { generated: "scripts/nxm-live-routes.ts", exact: [...exact].sort(), patterns };
writeFileSync(join(ROOT, "app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json"), JSON.stringify(out, null, 1) + "\n");
console.log(`live-routes.json: ${out.exact.length} exact routes, ${patterns.length} patterns`);

content.thinking:
Since there's no project-id column locally, I can't resolve dependency names from the DB directly. Instead I'll fetch them live via a single bulk Modrinth API call for project ids, throttled and cached through the safe-fetch helper.

The existing engine installer already resolves and installs required dependencies automatically, so "one-click install with dependencies" just reuses that flow; optional deps get their own install buttons when they're already in the catalog. For client-required detection, K3's client_side column isn't guaranteed to exist in Prisma's typed schema, so I'd need to fall back to a raw query or check if the column is present before showing any client-required warning.

I'll read optional fields defensively by casting the returned row to an untyped record, so once K3 merges its columns and the client regenerates, those fields just come through automatically without any schema coupling on my end. Since gallery support already exists via galleryKeys/galleryUrls, I don't need a separate ModMedia model — I'll stick to three additive models: ModVerification for check results, a ModSmokeTest queue model, and a ModBlockedHash model for tracking known-bad hashes by sha256/sha512 with reason and addedBy fields.

For ModVerification, I'm designing fields like gameModId, modVersionId, versionNumber snapshot, gameFamily/gameVersion/loader, status, a JSON checks blob, verifiedAt/expiresAt, verifiedBy, notes, and revocation fields, with a unique constraint on (modVersionId, gameVersion, loader) and indexes for status lookups. Since smoke tests can't actually run in this environment yet, true VERIFIED status can't be achieved until the owner runs the runner — automated checks can execute now as a "preflight" that records results while leaving status at UNVERIFIED with the smoke test queued, keeping things honest rather than letting admins manually flip status. For screenshot purposes in the throwaway DB, I'll seed a few VERIFIED rows as fixtures simulating a passed smoke test.

Now I'm working out badge display logic: a card shows "Verified" when a non-expired VERIFIED row exists for the current game version, with a marketing variant showing "on 1.21.1" for any matched version. For expiry, I'm using 30 days or invalidation on game update, since Minecraft verification is per-game-version and a new version is simply unverified by default; for games without discrete versions I'd treat it as "latest" with a 30-day expiry, and I'm planning an `invalidateVerificationsForGame(family, reason)` helper to be called externally when a game update is detected, leaving the actual hook-in to whoever owns the game-update worker. For the checks module, I'm starting with a pure, testable license check that determines whether the license permits use or redistribution.

I'm deciding to be conservative on the license check: pass only when the license is a recognized OSI/CC-style redistributable SPDX license, and fail for ARR, custom, or unknown licenses, even though this excludes popular ARR mods, since the task specifically requires redistribution/use rights and fetch-through installation doesn't clearly satisfy that under a strict reading. The second check verifies the source is from an allowlisted provider (Modrinth, Hangar, Thunderstore, uMod, GitHub, Factorio mod portal, Ficsit, possibly CurseForge) with the file URL host matching the known mod hosts list. The third check verifies the downloaded file's hash matches the upstream-declared sha512/sha1, which requires network access, so I'm planning to implement it as an async check in the runner with an injectable fetcher for testability.

For the remaining checks: archive safety needs to inspect zip/jar bytes for zip-slip traversal, entry count/size limits, and flag disallowed executable types per game (allowing .jar for Minecraft, .dll for Valheim/BepInEx, but flagging .exe/.bat/.sh/.ps1 everywhere); known-bad hashes get checked against a ModBlockedHash table; metadata completeness checks for required fields like name, description, license, author, icon, game version, file URL, and size; and version compatibility checks whether the ModVersion's declared gameVersions include the target version for versioned game families, treating unversioned families as not-applicable passes.

I'm defining the overall status logic: VERIFIED only when every check and the install smoke test pass and nothing's expired, FLAGGED when a hard failure occurs (bad hash, unsafe archive, hash mismatch), and UNVERIFIED otherwise. For the network side, I'm planning a preflight runner that downloads files via safeFetch from allowlisted hosts to populate real check results, and now I'm thinking about where this would run in production — likely as a background job or triggered by an admin "Run checks" button.

Rather than touching the worker, I'll have admin actions enqueue rows in a queue table (ModVerifyTask) with kind PREFLIGHT or SMOKE, which a separate runner script processes on demand, with a worker hook as a possible later addition. I'm sketching out the models: ModVerification for results and ModVerifyTask as the queue with fields for kind, target mod/version, game version, loader, and status.

Now I'm thinking about search performance over a large catalog — the existing ILIKE-based search would benefit from a trigram index, but Prisma's schema can't express a GIN trgm index directly, and since this repo uses `db push` rather than migrations, I'm uncertain whether a raw SQL index would survive a push or get dropped during introspection.

Actually, I recall Prisma 4+ does support declaring GIN indexes with trigram ops for PostgreSQL directly in the schema, requiring the pg_trgm extension to be enabled via the postgres extensions preview feature.

I should check whether pg_trgm is actually installed in production first, and before making any changes, run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the live prod database for a representative search query like "sodium" to establish a baseline.

Each search is taking around 140ms plus a separate count query, and pg_trgm isn't installed, which would require superuser access I probably don't have. I'm considering built-in Postgres full-text search with a GIN index on a tsvector instead, since that avoids needing extensions, though Prisma's schema support for generated columns is limited.

Actually, pg_trgm has been a trusted extension since PG13, meaning any role with CREATE privilege on the database can install it without superuser—so db push might just work if the nxeon role has that permission, though enabling the postgresqlExtensions preview feature could have broader implications for client generation.

A safer route might be a standalone SQL script the owner runs separately to create the extension and index, but I need to verify whether Prisma's db push treats unrecognized indexes as drift and drops them—I should test this on a throwaway database to be sure.

Alternatively, I could sidestep the performance issue by skipping the exact count when a search query is present, since the count doubles query time and an estimated "has more" check would suffice. For now, I'll set up the throwaway DB to actually test the drop behavior.

For getModPreview, I'm designing it to fetch a GameMod row plus its latest 30 ModVersion rows, compute per-version compat against the target server, parse dependency data (which differs in shape between Modrinth and Hangar), and resolve those dependencies to local GameMod rows. Since Modrinth dependencies reference project IDs rather than slugs, I'll need to call the Modrinth API to resolve IDs to slugs/titles (cached for an hour, using the allowlisted fetch wrapper) and then look up matching local rows by family and source.

I'm also handling graceful fallback when dependency resolution fails (just showing the raw ID), and figuring out the body rendering pipeline: prefer stored sanitized HTML, fall back to rendering markdown, then plain description, all passed through a hardening function to enforce the HTML allowlist. For gallery and external links, I'm mapping over the stored keys and various URL columns (source, project page, license, issues, discord, wiki, donation links).

For author display and client-side requirement, I only want to surface fields when the data actually exists rather than guessing — Modrinth's client_side field wasn't captured in the older schema, so I'll leave it undefined unless present. I also want to pull verification rows, per-version changelogs rendered and truncated, plus license, file size, download count, and last-updated timestamp with sensible fallbacks between stored and upstream values.

I'm sketching a small `opt<T>` helper to safely read optional columns, and thinking through caching strategy — a short-lived in-memory count cache plus considering whether the marketing preview should use a longer-lived cache mechanism.

Now I'm designing the HTML sanitizer: it needs to tokenize tags, strip anything not on an explicit allowlist while preserving inner text, but fully remove dangerous tags like script/style/iframe along with their contents. For attributes, I'm restricting things to safe ones like class, validated href/src, alt, title, loading, a locked-down target, and a rewritten rel value.

I'll split the input by the tag regex, escaping `<` and `>` in plain text segments while leaving `&` untouched, then rebuild any matched tags using only the allowlist.

For attributes, I need a regex capturing name/value pairs with quoted or unquoted values, then validate href strictly against `^https://` or a safe root-relative path `^/` to block `javascript:` and entity-encoded bypasses like `javascript:`, since literal prefix matching defeats those tricks.

When re-emitting the escaped attribute string, I realize I must only escape quotes and angle brackets, not ampersands, since the markdown escaping already produced `&` and double-escaping would corrupt URLs — entities decoded inside an attribute value happen after tokenization so they can't break out of the quotes.

(`ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS=1`, loaded by the worker unit), but the Mods tab only ever loaded the top 400

from `appliesToVariant` alone, so Fabric mods offered Install on Paper servers. The Minecraft installer

`curl` whatever URL an API returned; Valheim installs didn't check for the BepInEx server type and ignored

authentication methods failed").

Built: `lib/mods/` (engine, safe-fetch, archive, paths, mirror, guest-fs, queue, facts) +
`lib/mods/installers/{minecraft,valheim,rust,cs2,factorio,index}.ts`, `worker/mods-guest-ssh.ts`

## NX Labs catalog ingestion, local mod mirror and /admin/nxlabs (2026-10-01)

**Why.** `GameMod` held ~64,000 rows (Minecraft 32k, Factorio 5.4k, Vintage Story 3.9k, Space Engineers 2.2k,
~20 other families at ~1k each) but only a weekly shell timer (`scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh`, never
installed) refreshed it, rows carried no per-version/compatibility data, images were hotlinked, and no file was
ever stored locally. Audit of prod (read-only, 2026-10-01): Minecraft is rich (icon 100%, versions 100%,
license 99.9%, gallery 66%), but most Steam-Workshop families have 0% versions/license/long description,
Rust has only 30 rows (uMod importer deliberately unscheduled, Cloudflare-blocked ToS), CS:GO/CS 1.6 9 rows,
Terraria 23, 11 duplicated (family, source, sourceId) groups.

  with jitter, Retry-After, ETag/If-Modified-Since), `license.ts` (redistribution allow-list), `store.ts` (idempotent

  nulls; sanitised HTML via `lib/mod-markdown.ts`), `images.ts` (sharp -> WebP, content-addressed, served by
  `app/api/nxlabs/img/[key]/route.ts`), `mirror.ts`, `runner.ts` (resumable bounded slices, DB claim, run history),
  `registry.ts`, `urls.ts` (`modIconSrc`/`modGallerySrc` helpers for UIs). Native providers: **modrinth**,
  **hangar**, **factorio**, **ficsit**; each exports pure parsers tested against recorded fixtures
  (`test/fixtures/modsync/*`, `test/modsync.test.ts`).
- Worker: `worker/modsync.ts` `modsyncTick()` hooked into `worker/index.ts` (fire-and-forget every 5 min; one bounded
  slice <= 6 min of the next due provider; cursor saved in `ModSyncProvider`). `MODSYNC_DISABLED=1` turns it off.

content.content:
1. Cheat gate, `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()`: `if (m_cheat) { if ((bool)ZNet.instance) return ZNet.instance.IsServer(); return false; } return false;`. `m_cheat` is a `public static bool` on `Terminal`, so it is per process.
2. `devcommands`: `new ConsoleCommand("devcommands", "enables cheats", args => { if ((bool)ZNet.instance && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()) ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand("devcommands"); m_cheat = !m_cheat; ... "Dev commands: " + m_cheat ... }, isCheat: false, isNetwork: false, onlyServer: false, isSecret: true)`. On a client it flips the client's `m_cheat` and also forwards the command.
3. Forwarding: `ZNet.RemoteCommand(cmd)` invokes RPC `"RPC_RemoteCommand"`, which is registered only `if (m_isServer)`. Server side: `RPC_RemoteCommand(rpc, command) { if (!ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())) RemotePrint(rpc, "You are not admin"); else InternalCommand(rpc, command); }` and `InternalCommand` logs `"Remote admin '" + hostName + "' executed command '" + command + "' remotely."` then calls `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)`, running the command in the SERVER's console. So Jay's three `devcommands` flipped the server's `m_cheat` on, off, on. His client's `m_cheat` ended `true` too. That only helps commands the server itself runs.
4. Dispatch, `Terminal.TryRunCommand`: `if (cmd.IsValid(this)) cmd.RunAction(...); else if (cmd.RemoteCommand && (bool)ZNet.instance && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()) ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text); else AddString("'" + name + "' is not valid in the current context.");`. An unknown name gives `"'x' is not a recognized command. Type 'help' to see a list of valid commands."`. Jay's "unknown" is the first message. The command exists but is refused locally.
5. `ConsoleCommand.IsValid`: `(!IsCheat || context.IsCheatsEnabled()) && (context.isAllowedCommand(this) || skip) && (!IsNetwork || ZNet.instance)`, then `if (OnlyServer) return ZNet.instance.IsServer();`. Note that the `ConsoleEventFailable` constructor sets `OnlyServer = onlyServer || onlyAdmin`. The `OnlyAdmin` field is never read anywhere else in the assembly.
6. Registration flags: `god`, `ghost`, `heal`: `isCheat: true, onlyServer: false, remoteCommand: false, onlyAdmin: true` (void delegate, so OnlyServer stays false). `fly`, `debugmode`, `nocost`, `exploremap`: `isCheat: true, onlyServer: true`, not remote. `spawn`: `onlyAdmin: true` with a failable delegate, so effectively OnlyServer. Forwarded (`remoteCommand: true`): `confirmcheats`, `genloc`, `players`, `setkey`, `removekey`, `resetkeys`, `resetworldkeys`, `setworldpreset`, `setworldmodifier`, `listkeys`, `sleep`, `skiptime`, `restartparty`. `kick`/`ban`/`unban` are not cheats and work for admins with no mod (their RPCs check `ListContainsId` on the server).
7. Admin status on a client: the server sends RPC `AdminList` (the full list) to every peer on connect. The client stores it in `m_adminListForRpc`, and `GetAdminList()` returns it. `LocalPlayerIsAdminOrHost()` = `IsServer() || GetAdminList().Contains(UserInfo.GetLocalUser().UserId.ToString())`. `PlatformUserID.ToString()` (Splatform) = `"Steam_" + id`. The server's own `ListContainsId` accepts both `Steam_<id>` and the bare `<id>`. So with a bare-ID adminlist, which is what the lloesche `ADMINLIST_IDS` env writes, the server treats Jay as admin and his own client does not.

**Why 1.0.0 failed.** Its only patch was a postfix on `IsCheatsEnabled` returning true when `m_cheat && LocalPlayerIsAdminOrHost()`. On the server, `IsServer()` is true, so vanilla already returns `m_cheat` and the patch never changes anything. On a client it was never installed. Even if it had been, it would fail twice: `fly`/`debugmode`/`spawn` are also `OnlyServer`, and with a bare-ID adminlist `LocalPlayerIsAdminOrHost()` is false. The harness confirms all of this (below).

**Fix: NxeonDevAdmin 2.0.0** (`tools/valheim-plugins/NxeonDevAdmin/Plugin.cs`, DLL `worker/assets/valheim/NxeonDevAdmin.dll`, sha256 `da421fb10f692f207d8110d26b7f5ba90a113424202f84813bd277387c721747`). Built against the real l-1.0.16 DLLs and BepInExPack 5.4.2351. All three changes apply only on a client whose user is in the synced admin list, with either ID form accepted:
1. `IsCheatsEnabled` postfix: true when `m_cheat`.
2. `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` postfix: `OnlyServer` commands that are not `RemoteCommand` may run locally. Remote commands keep the vanilla forwarding. `isAllowedCommand` is still called, so chat refuses cheats.
3. Sets `Game.isModded = true`, which also skips the `confirmcheats` prompt.

On the server it is a no-op, so it stays mounted there unchanged. Other players never need it.

**Verification.** `tools/valheim-plugins/NxeonDevAdmin.Harness/run.sh` loads the real `assembly_valheim.dll` in .NET 8 and registers the real commands through `Terminal.InitTerminal()`. It then drives the real `TryRunCommand` as a remote client: `m_isServer=false`, a synced admin list, Jay's ID. Only Unity-native calls are stubbed (UnityEngine.Object bool/== operators, `AddString`, `RunAction` bodies, the RPC send, the Steam user lookup). Results:
- Vanilla client: `god`/`ghost`/`fly`/`debugmode`/`nocost`/`spawn`/`heal`/`exploremap` all print `'<cmd>' is not valid in the current context.` (this reproduces Jay's symptom). `sleep`/`skiptime`/`listkeys` are forwarded to the server.
- Client with 1.0.0, bare-ID adminlist: identical to vanilla (`IsCheatsEnabled` stays false).
- Client with 1.0.0, `Steam_` adminlist: `god`/`ghost`/`heal` unlock, but `fly`/`debugmode`/`nocost`/`spawn`/`exploremap` are still refused.
- Client with 2.0.0, bare or prefixed adminlist: all eight run locally. Remote commands are still forwarded. Chat still refuses cheats.
- Client with 2.0.0, not on the adminlist: everything refused, as in vanilla.
- Server process: `IsCheatsEnabled` is unchanged.

`test/valheim-devadmin-dll.test.ts` (`npm test`) statically checks that the committed DLL has version 2.0.0 and both patch targets.

**Not proven (needs a real game client):** that BepInEx loads the DLL alongside Jay's 23 mods; that no other mod patches the same two methods in a conflicting way; and that the command bodies (Unity-native) behave on a client. For `fly`/`debugmode`/`god` this is the normal single-player code path, and other "server devcommands" mods rely on the same thing. Also unverified: that the lloesche `ADMINLIST_IDS` env overwrites `adminlist.txt`, which matters if a customer adds `Steam_` lines by hand.

**Changed in this branch:** plugin source and csproj (adds the `Splatform` reference and a `RefsDir` property), README, harness + `run.sh`, the static test, the built DLL, `worker/game-config.ts` (comment, plus removal of the two customer notes claiming "admins can now use devcommands, no extra mod needed"), the `lib/game-config.ts` `ADMINLIST_IDS` help text, and the Valheim KB rows (Own plugin, Playbook 6, compatibility traps, reply template 5, runbook console line).

import { SPR, APP } from "@/lib/nx/sprites";
import { NX_ICONS, NX_ICON_TONE, type NxTone } from "@/lib/nx/icon-paths";

/* ── one dial for icon size, site-wide ────────────────────────────────────
   Every mark in the system is drawn a fixed multiple of the size its call site
   asks for. Applying it HERE rather than editing hundreds of call sites keeps
   the relative sizing intact: an icon that was deliberately smaller than its
   neighbour stays proportionally smaller, it is just bigger in absolute terms.
   Change this one number to retune the whole set.

   Note for anyone adding a primitive: scale exactly ONCE per rendered mark.
   `Plate` draws an `Icon` inside itself, so it scales its own BOX and passes
   the raw size through — scaling in both places would compound to 2.25x. */
export const ICON_SCALE = 1.5;
export const iconPx = (n: number) => Math.round(n * ICON_SCALE);

/**
 * One interface mark.
 *
 * VECTOR FIRST, sprite as the fallback. `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` carries the set
 * redrawn as 24x24 paths; anything it defines renders as an inline SVG in
 * `currentColor`, and anything it doesn't — the sheet's brand row (linux,
 * docker, postgres…) and the five 3D product renders — still comes off
 * `public/nx/nxicons.webp` exactly as before.
 *
 * Why the switch is here rather than at 137 call sites: the sprite's marks are
 * pre-coloured, so one inside a tinted control renders in the SHEET's colour
 * instead of the control's (a teal shieldcheck on a violet "Admin" chip is the
 * bug that started this). Routing both through one component means every call
 * site gets `currentColor` without being edited, and a name with no vector yet
 * silently keeps working.
 *
 * `size` still means what it always did — ICON_SCALE is applied here for BOTH
 * paths, so a swap is 1:1 and `Plate` (which sizes its box with `iconPx`)
 * needs no change.
 */
ActivityAurora.tsx
ActivityView.tsx
AuroraBg.tsx
Banners.tsx
BillingAurora.tsx
BillingView.tsx
Bits.tsx

content.content:
Separate ZFS backup poolsnapshots kept off your server’s own disks
Isolation

A real machine boundary between tenants

The strongest isolation on the platform is the default one: every customer gets a full virtual machine, not a slice of a shared container.

Full KVM virtual machines

Every customer runs inside a full KVM virtual machine with hardware-assisted virtualization, not a shared container carved out of someone else’s kernel. You get a real, isolated machine boundary.

Network and DDoS

The blast radius stops at your VM

Our network is built so a compromised or attacked server can’t become everyone else’s problem, starting with a firewall that refuses to let VMs talk to the host.

Management plane walled off

The host firewall drops all traffic from customer VMs to the host. Even a fully compromised server can’t reach our hypervisor, management plane or database. The blast radius stops at your VM.

Data safety

Backups that survive a bad day

Redundant, self-healing storage for your live data, plus automatic snapshots kept somewhere separate, so a single failure or fat-fingered command isn’t the end of the story.

Snapshots to a separate pool

Automatic snapshots stream to a separate ZFS backup pool, kept off your server’s own disks, so your data can survive a mistake, a bad deploy or a full host failure.

Account security

Lock down the front door

Strong infrastructure only matters if your account is hard to break into. These are the controls guarding access to everything you run on Nxeon.

Two-factor authentication

Protect your account with TOTP-based 2FA from any authenticator app, so a leaked or reused password alone can never be enough to reach your servers.

<
Ownership and privacy

Your data belongs to you

Trust cuts both ways: you should be able to leave as easily as you arrived. We build for portability, not for lock-in.

Your data is yours

You get full root on your own server. What you run and what you store belongs to you. We don’t rummage through your VMs and we don’t sell your data.

Transparent billing

The same honesty, applied to money

Security is trust, and so is billing. We price plainly, show real renewal costs, and make leaving a single click, because a customer who can walk away is one we have to keep earning.

Clear, upfront pricing

The price on the page is the price you pay. No mandatory add-ons hidden at checkout and no surprise line items on your first invoice.

Honest rene

What we don’t claim

We won’t put a badge on this page we haven’t earned. Everything above describes controls that are live today. If a compliance program matters for your workload, talk to us about where we’re headed.

NOT HELDSOC 2Nxeon does not currently hold a SOC 2 report.
NOT HELDISO 27001Nxeon is not currently ISO 27001 certified.
NOT HELDPCI DSSCard details are handled by our payment processor, and Nxeon does not hold its own PCI certification.

Deploy your first server in under a minute

Creating an account is free and takes no card details. You pay when you deploy: choose a billing term and pay from your wallet or by card at checkout.

{{SPRITE}} {{NAV}}

NX Labs mod library

Nxeon Verified: mods we have actually run

Every mod in our library installs in one click. Some also carry the Nxeon Verified badge, which means we installed that exact build on a fresh test server, started the game with it, watched it load, and checked its licence and file integrity. Here is exactly what the badge means, and what it doesn’t.

Browse the mod libraryDeploy a game server
What it saysWhat we checkHow it stays freshWhat it isn’tFAQ
The exact wording

One sentence, and we stand behind every word of it

The badge is earned by one build of one mod, on one game version, and the panel behind it says precisely that. It never claims more than the test proved.

Nxeon Verified: installed and started successfully on <game> <version> on <date>; licence and file integrity checked.

What we check

Eight checks, all of them, every time

Seven run automatically against the file itself. The eighth is the one that matters most: a real install on a real, throwaway game server. A build has to pass all eight to earn the badge.

Installed and started

We create a fresh test server of the right game and version, install the build with the same one-click installer you use, restart the game, and read its own log to confirm the server came up and the mod loaded. Then the test server is deleted.

Licence permits use

The project must publish an open licence that allows use and redistribution. “All rights reserved” or no licence at all means no badge, however popular the mod is.

File integrity

We download the file and compare its checksum with the one the mod’s own source publishes. A mismatch flags the build for review straight away.

Approved source

Files must come over HTTPS from the official download host of a source we support, such as Modrinth, Hangar, Thunderstore, uMod, GitHub releases or the Factorio mod portal.

Archive safety

Archives are opened and inspected: no paths that escape their folder, no links, no oversized or compression-bomb entries, and no executable or script types that don’t belong in that game’s mods.

Known-bad list

The file’s hash is checked against our list of files we’ve pulled. Adding a hash to that list revokes every badge for that file at once.

Declared compatibility

The build must state that it supports the exact game version and loader it was tested on, so the badge is never stretched to a version nobody tried.

Complete listing

Name, summary, author, licence, icon, version and file details must all be present, so you know what you’re installing before you install it.

Freshness

A badge that can’t go stale

Mods and games both update constantly, so a verification is tied to the exact build and game version it was earned on, and it lapses on its own.

  1. Per build

    A new release of the mod is a new file. It starts unverified and has to pass every check again.

  2. Per game version

    Passing on Minecraft 1.21.1 says nothing about 1.21.4, so the badge only shows to servers on the version that was tested.

  3. Expires in 30 days

    Every badge carries an expiry date. When it passes, the badge disappears until the build is tested again.

  4. Revoked instantly

    If a build misbehaves after it was verified, we pull the badge at once, and it stays down until a new test passes.

What the badge doesn’t claim

We would rather under-promise. The badge describes a test we ran and the result we saw, nothing more. Mods without it still install in one click; most of the library simply hasn’t been through a test run yet, and that is not a warning about them.

NOT CLAIMEDA security auditWe don’t read or review a mod’s source code, and the badge is not a malware guarantee.
NOT CLAIMEDWorks with every other modEach build is tested on its own. Combinations with other mods aren’t covered.
NOT CLAIMEDAn endorsementVerification says the build ran. It says nothing about whether it suits your server or your players.
FAQ

Questions, answered

Is a mod without the badge unsafe?

No. The badge is new and testing happens one build and one game version at a time, so most of the library hasn’t been through it yet. Every mod still installs in one click, from its own source, with its checksum checked by the installer.

Where do I see the badge?

On mod cards and in the mod preview inside your server’s Mods & Plugins tab. It only appears when the verified build matches your server’s game version and loader. Click it to see every check and the date it ran.

Can I filter for verified mods only?

Yes. The mod browser has a “Nxeon Verified only” switch next to “Fits my server”.

Does Nxeon Verified mean the mod is secure?

No. It is a compatibility and integrity check: the file is what its source published, it is structurally safe to unpack, its licence allows use, and it installed and started on a test server. It is not a review of the mod’s code.

How long does a verification last?

30 days, or until the mod or the game updates, whichever comes first. After that the badge disappears until the build is tested again.

What happens if a verified mod causes problems?

Tell us through support. We can revoke a badge immediately, and adding the file’s hash to our known-bad list removes the badge from every verification of that file.

Your server, your mods, one click

Pick a game, deploy in under a minute, then browse the mod library from your server’s Mods tab, with the builds that fit your server shown first.

Deploy a game serverBrowse mods
{{FOOTER}}

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

I found the actual bug: the Install button overlaps the popover because the card's bottom row and the chip row are sibling elements both using the same z-index, so the later one in DOM order paints on top. +  clientSide      String?

+  /// Every author/team member: [{ name, url?, avatarUrl?, role? }].

+  /// Cross-provider dedupe: when set, this row is a DUPLICATE of the canonical row with that id and is
+  /// hidden from customer listings (duplicateOfId = null means canonical or unique). See docs/MODS-SOURCES.md.
+  duplicateOfId   String?
+  /// Normalised identity key the dedupe pass grouped on (e.g. "gh:owner/repo" or "nm:slug-author").
+  dedupeKey       String?
+  media           ModMedia[]
+
+  @@index([dedupeKey])
+  @@index([duplicateOfId])
+  @@index([gameFamily, source])
+}
+
+/// Rich media for one GameMod (icon, screenshots, banner). `key` = our cached webp (served by
+/// /api/nxlabs/img/<key>); rows without a key are served via the hotlink-safe proxy /api/nxlabs/media/<id>.
+model ModMedia {
+  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
+  gameModId   String
+  gameMod     GameMod  @relation(fields: [gameModId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
+  /// icon | screenshot | banner | video
+  kind        String   @default("screenshot")
+  url         String
+  key         String?
+  title       String?
+  description String?
+  ordinal     Int      @default(0)
+  /// True when the licence allowed us to persist a copy in the NX Labs store.
+  mirrored    Boolean  @default(false)
+  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
+
+  @@unique([gameModId, url])
+  @@index([gameModId, kind, ordinal])
+  // ── mod-providers-massive (additive) ──
+  /// Normalised dependency list: [{ kind: required|optional|incompatible|embedded, source, projectId, name?, versionId? }].
+  depList        Json?
+  /// Per-version side requirements (required|optional|unsupported) when the provider has them.
+  clientSide     String?
+  serverSideReq  String?
+  /// Provider-declared release date of the primary file's last change is publishedAt; size in fileBytes.

# K5 modui — mod browser, preview modal, Nxeon Verified (2026-10-01)

input.message:
**K5 modui: mod browser, preview modal and Nxeon Verified are done on branch `feature/mod-browser-verified` (worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-modui`). No production mod shows the badge yet: the real install test (smoke test) has never run, and you start it.**

Commits: 514717024e (verification core + data layer), 6e76805d8f (UI, admin, runner, /mods/verified), b4f56400db (fixes from screenshot review), 6105a70615 (merge of main, which already contained K3's work), ae5b2e2cb8 (docs).

**What's built**
- **Browser** in the server's Mods & Plugins tab (`components/customer/mods/browser/*`):
  - Search runs in the database, 24 per page, with a 250 ms debounce.
  - Filters: category, game version, loader, sort. "Fits my server" is on by default. There is also a "Nxeon Verified only" switch.
  - Cards show compat for this server, install state and the badge, with loading, empty and error states.
  - Data access is in `lib/mods-browse.ts` and `lib/actions-mod-browse.ts`. Both check that the user owns the server.
- **Preview modal**:
  - Opens from a card or a `?mod=slug` link. It traps focus, closes on Esc, and becomes a bottom sheet on mobile.
  - Gallery with lightbox, using K3's `ModMedia` first, then K2's gallery columns.
  - The description is sanitised twice: the existing `lib/mod-markdown.ts` renderer, then a new allow-list pass in `lib/mod-html-harden.ts`, tested against XSS inputs.
  - Tabs for versions (fit per version), changelog and dependencies (required / optional / incompatible).
  - Shows links, licence, authors, and a "players need it too" warning when the mod requires it client-side.
  - Install / Update / Remove use the existing installer actions.
- **Nxeon Verified** (`lib/mod-verify/*`):
  - Badge copy: "installed and started successfully on <game> <version> on <date>; licence and file integrity checked". The popover says it is not a security audit.
  - It applies per mod build and game version. It requires seven automatic checks plus the install test.
  - It expires after 30 days. It disappears once a newer build exists for that game version. Admins can revoke it, and blocking a file hash revokes every verification of that file.
- **Runner** `scripts/mod-verify.ts`, run by you only: `queue`, `preflight`, `smoke --plan`, `smoke --confirm --region <r>`, `lapse`. The smoke step refuses any region that contains the primary node and always deletes its test server.
- **Admin queue** at `/admin/nxlabs/verified` (ADMIN only, audited): stats, bulk revoke / flag / reset, task queue, known-bad hash list.
- **Public page** `/mods/verified` built as a native nxm page; it emits FAQPage structured data. Mod detail pages show the badge only from a live verification. The old `verifiedAt` tick is relabelled "Source-checked".

**Schema** (additive, no relations onto GameMod/ModVersion): `ModVerification`, `ModVerifyTask`, `ModBlockedHash`. I didn't add a media table; K3's `ModMedia` is used.

**How it was checked**
- Typecheck is clean after the merge. 24 new tests in `test/mod-verify.test.ts` pass, along with the existing modsync and installer tests.
- Playwright ran against a dev server on a throwaway DB (now dropped) seeded with 450 real catalogue mods. Confirmed: deep link opens the modal, focus stays trapped, Esc closes the lightbox and modal, no horizontal overflow on mobile, and the explainer page and mod detail return 200.
- Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/modui/shots/` (01–51: grid, verified-only, popover, empty, skeleton, error, modal tabs, lightbox, mobile sheet, light mode, Valheim, admin, `/mods/verified`). Bugs found in them were fixed: the popover was drawn under the next card, icons had no fallback, the search box had two clear buttons, light-mode chips had poor contrast.
- Preflight checks ran for real against 23 builds downloaded from Modrinth; 3 passed. The three VERIFIED rows in the screenshots come from a fake install test on that throwaway DB, not a real one.

**Not verified / open**
- No real install test has run. To start: `npx tsx scripts/mod-verify.ts queue --family minecraft --game-version 1.21.1 --loader paper`, then `preflight`, `smoke --plan`, then `smoke --confirm --region <non-primary> --limit 1`.
- `lapseForGameUpdate()` isn't called from the game-update worker yet; that's R's area.
- Search is ~95–140 ms per query on prod data. A `pg_trgm` index would fix it, but `prisma db push` drops raw SQL indexes (I checked on the throwaway DB), so it's your call.
- The built-in sanitiser is used because a new npm package can't be installed into the shared `node_modules`.
- Load-detection log patterns exist only for Minecraft, Valheim and Rust. Other games come back as "can't confirm".

**Files edited outside my area**
- `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/ModsPanel.tsx` (K1): the Browse tab now uses the new browser.
- `app/admin/nxlabs/page.tsx`: one link to the queue.
- `app/nxm/_data/mod-lithium.ts` and `mods-lib.ts`: badge and relabel.
- `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py`, `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`, `app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts`, `live-routes.json`: the new route.
- `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Still saying a plain "Verified" in other owners' files: `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`, `components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, `app/nxm/_data/games-lib.ts`.

**Risk:** Postgres hit its connection limit during this session (the throwaway DB at `/opt/nxeon-wt-modproviders` alone held 39 of 100). I capped my own dev server at 5 connections.

Notes are in `/root/agent-notes/modui.md`.
